ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, objects A and B are connected by a light string and a spring and then pass over a pulley. A is at rest on a rough inclined plane with an inclination angle of $45^{\circ}$, and B is hanging. It is known that the masses satisfy $m_A=3m_B$, and pulley friction is neglected. Now the inclination angle of the inclined plane is decreased from $45^{\circ}$ to $30^{\circ}$, and A is always at rest relative to the inclined plane. Then which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The static friction force on object A will decrease

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, object A is placed on a rough inclined plane, and the inclined plane is marked 45°; A is connected through a light string/spring upward along the inclined plane to a fixed pulley near the upper end of the inclined plane, and after the string passes over the pulley, object B is hanging on the right side. B hangs vertically, pulley friction is neglected, and A remains at rest relative to the inclined plane. Reasoning: First look at the vertical equilibrium of B. When B is at rest, in the vertical direction it is subject to gravity m_B g and the tension T of the string/spring, so T=m_B g. Then write the equilibrium for A along the direction of the inclined plane. A is subject to the component of gravity m_A g sinθ downward along the inclined plane and the tension T upward along the inclined plane. It is known that m_A=3m_B, so the component of gravity along the inclined plane is 3m_B g sinθ. When θ=45°, m_A g sin45°=3m_B g·√2/2, which is greater than T=m_B g, so A has a tendency to slide down along the inclined plane, and the static friction force is upward along the inclined plane, with magnitude f_45=m_A g sin45°−T=(3√2/2−1)m_B g. When θ=30°, m_A g sin30°=3m_B g·1/2=1.5m_B g, which is also greater than T=m_B g, so A still has a tendency to slide down along the inclined plane, and the static friction force is still upward along the inclined plane, with magnitude f_30=m_A g sin30°−T=(3/2−1)m_B g=0.5m_B g. By comparison, (3√2/2−1)m_B g≈1.12m_B g, which is greater than 0.5m_B g, so after the inclination angle of the inclined plane is decreased from 45° to 30°, the static friction force on A decreases.
